newsitem.title: PERU: Rebel women among Peru hostage-takers.
newsitem.headline: Rebel women among Peru hostage-takers.

text.p: Two or three of the Marxist rebels holding hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence are women, according to reports on Sunday by former captives of the commandos and by photographers using long-view lenses to see faces in the windows of the compound.
"I am very sad ... it is lamentable that two 16-year-old women are in the (rebel) group," said Spanish Jesuit priest Luis Martinez, who was freed after three days of captivity.
Photographers say they have also seen rebel women at windows of the besieged residence. Women captives were all released shortly after the guerrillas occupied the building last Tuesday.
The women rebels' participation highlighted the strong female role in Peru's guerrillas, in sharp contrast to its generally macho, male-dominated society.

"It is not the first time the MRTA (Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement) has used women in its commando-type operations. In each operation there are always one or two women who generally have a lesser-ranking role," one anti-terrorist police source said on Sunday.
The MRTA's most famous alleged member is American woman Lori Berenson, 27, serving a life sentence at the 13,000 feet (3,960 metres) high Yanamayo maximum security prison in Puno, southern Peru.

She was accused of plotting last year an aborted rebel takeover of the Peruvian Congress, helping to psychologically prepare guerrilla fighters and gathering intelligence by posing as a journalist for U.S.-based magazines.
One of the top imprisoned MRTA leaders serving a life sentence, Lucero Cumpa, is also a woman.
Women have played an even greater role in Peru's larger and bloodier guerrilla group the Shining Path, holding top leadership posts.
In 1992 along with the capture of the Maoist group's chief, Abimael Guzman, the police caught and jailed three women from Shining Path's central organising commmittee.
